title: Model the side the learner didn't pick
statement: In an argument task, let the worked example argue the side the learner did not pick, so it models the reasoning without handing over their case.
example: The model case has three parts, an answer, its proof and why the proof proves it, and the learner's own case uses the same three.
detail: The Grade 9 prototype has the learner pick a side after reading, then shows the guide's own case, a worked example in three parts (an answer, the proof and why it proves it) that argues the side the learner did not pick, and closes it by inviting the learner to beat it with a case of the same three parts built from two of their own marked lines. An earlier design canvas offers the same move as on-demand help, a strong reader arguing the opposite case for one paragraph, and the research brief behind the design suggests a rival reader whose weaker claim the student beats as a plausible way to build confidence, which it marks as its own inference. Nothing in the sources measures the effect.

evidence.quote: 4. **Pick a side**, after reading, with the marked lines in view.
